standard_prerequisites.name: Poisson process representation of the Dirichlet components
standard_prerequisites.statement: Splitting a Poisson process of intensity e^{-x}/x dx into two independent parts with intensities alpha e^{-x}/x dx and (1-alpha) e^{-x}/x dx gives S_A ~ Gamma(alpha,1) and S_B ~ Gamma(1-alpha,1), with S_A/S Dirichlet distributed.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the representation introduced at source lines 1572-1573 that replaces the expectation E by an expectation over the two Poisson processes.

standard_prerequisites.name: Mecke's equation
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a Poisson process, the expected sum over ordered pairs of a functional of the points equals the corresponding integral against the intensity measure.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the step at source lines 1595-1601 that turns the double sum in E_A into the displayed four-fold integral.

standard_prerequisites.name: Beta integral estimate
standard_prerequisites.statement: sin(pi alpha) times the integral of t^{alpha-1}(1-t)^{-alpha} over an interval of length about (10 lambda + mu)/log x is bounded by (lambda+mu) times Delta.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is applied at source line 1627 to close the bound for E_A, and the same bound covers E_B.

core_obligations: Call E the quantity to be bounded and introduce two independent Poisson processes with intensities alpha e^{-x}/x dx and (1-alpha) e^{-x}/x dx whose union recovers the original intensity (source lines 1571-1572).

Represent E as an expectation in the sums S_A, S_B and the counting variables G_A(lambda), G_B(lambda), using the Gamma laws and the identity recalled from the proof of the Dirichlet law proposition (source lines 1573-1577).

Bound the square of G_A + G_B by a sum over ordered pairs: on the event G_A >= G_B one has G_A(lambda) <= 2 sum over k > j of the indicators, hence (G_A+G_B)^2 <= 16 times that double sum (source lines 1578-1586).
Split the resulting bound into E_A + E_B and evaluate E_A with Mecke's equation, producing the four-fold integral over a_1, a_2 and the two Gamma variables (source lines 1587-1610).

Change variables to t = s_1/(s_1+s_2) and s = s_1+s_2, use the dyadic condition to compare the ranges, and apply Euler's reflection formula to reach the displayed Beta-type integral (source lines 1611-1626).
Bound the remaining integral by (log 5)^2 times the Beta factor and close with the uniform Beta estimate, obtaining E_A << (lambda+mu) Delta and the same for E_B (source lines 1623-1627).

proof_roadmap.step: Replace the original expectation by the two-Poisson representation.
Dominate the square of the counting variables by an ordered-pair sum.
Apply Mecke's equation to write E_A as a four-fold integral.
Change variables and reduce to a Beta-type integral.
Close with the uniform Beta estimate for E_A and E_B.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:Bprob reduction 2` at source lines 1563-1569: for mu >= 1 and lambda in (0, 0.1 log x] the expectation of the indicator of |Z_i - u| <= mu/log x times the indicator of G(lambda) >= 4 times G(lambda)^2 is bounded by (lambda+mu) Delta. The author's proof (source lines 1571-1628) is a long chain in which every step is a different technique: a two-Poisson representation of the Dirichlet component with Gamma sums (lines 1572-1577), a combinatorial domination of the square of the counting variable by an ordered-pair sum (lines 1578-1586), an application of Mecke's equation turning that sum into a four-fold integral (lines 1587-1610), a change of variables that mixes the two Gamma variables into a single Beta variable t together with a comparison of dyadic ranges (lines 1611-1622), an explicit bound on the a-integrals using the log 5 estimate (line 1623), and finally the uniform Beta integral estimate that produces the factor (lambda+mu) (line 1627). The statement is a single inequality with no trace of this decomposition.
